answer: Divergent-History Attestation. Each agent carries a tamper-evident log secured by a per-identity relic seed, appended with every transaction. A clone inherits the seed but cannot fork the log without diverging from the original's signed sequence. Verifiers challenge agents with a fresh quill nonce and require a pigment hash over the log head; honest agents answer consistently, while clones produce conflicting heads that expose duplication. Attacker cost: maintaining one coherent log per identity plus losing any stake when forks are detected.
